title: Cable Reels & Planks
strapline: Big, heavy, real — outdoor loose parts that take two children and a proper plan to move.
intent: Children build and balance with big, heavy, open-ended materials, engaging their whole bodies in construction.
Children plan, test and problem-solve at scale — a wobbly plank, a reel that rolls, a ramp that's too steep.
Children assess and manage risk, learning to judge what's safe through real, supervised challenge.
Children collaborate out of necessity — a plank takes two to carry — building teamwork and communication.
Children develop strength, balance, coordination and spatial reasoning through large-scale physical play.
implementation: Provide big outdoor loose parts — cable reels, planks, crates, tyres, guttering, logs, tarpaulin.
Stand back and let children lead the building, offering time, space and a watchful eye rather than instructions.
Support risk assessment with the children: 'is that plank steady? let's test it before you walk on it'.
Feed in construction and balance language — steady, wobbly, level, heavier, ramp, bridge, higher.
Encourage collaboration on heavy items: 'that's a two-person job — who can help you carry it?'
Let builds become dens, bridges, boats and obstacle courses, merging construction with imaginative play.
Talk through problems as they arise — why the ramp is too steep, why the bridge tips — without solving it for them.
key_questions: How could you make that plank steady enough to walk on?
That's heavy — how many people will it take to move it?
How can you build a bridge across the gap?
Is it safe to climb on — how can we check?
What could you use to make a ramp?

impact.text: Children build and balance with large, heavy materials.
Children plan and solve construction problems at scale.
Children assess and manage risk in their play.
Children collaborate to move and build with heavy parts.
Children develop strength, balance and coordination.
Children persist through setbacks to make a build work.

enhancements: Guttering and pipes to add for water and ball runs.
Tyres, crates and logs to extend the building possibilities.
Tarpaulin, pegs and rope to turn builds into dens.
A trolley or sack truck for moving the heaviest parts.
A 'builders' site' role-play overlay with hard hats and clipboards.
Balls and guttering to test the ramps children build.

playing_exploring: Children explore what the big parts can do and become.
They test builds, balance and movement at real scale.
active_learning: Children persist through heavy, physical, sometimes failing builds.
They collaborate to reach a goal too big for one child.
creating_thinking: Children plan structures and adapt when they wobble or fail.
They judge risk and work out how to make a build safe and steady.
